correlates.name: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old man, former smoker, retired accountant on no regular drugs, has 14 months of slowly worsening exertional dyspnea and a dry cough; no rash, joint or muscle complaints. RR 22, SpO2 89% on room air; fine late-inspiratory crackles at both bases; clubbing.
correlates.workup: FVC 58% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.87, DLCO 38%. CT: subpleural, posterior-basal clustered cysts with reticular septal thickening and little hazy opacity. Surgical biopsy: patchy scar, dense old collagen beside pale nodules of plump fibroblasts.
correlates.management: Exclude drug, occupational and connective-tissue causes first; then refer for lung transplant evaluation, the only definitive therapy. Median survival is about 3.8 years from diagnosis.

correlates.name: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old woman who has never smoked has 7 months of exertional dyspnea and dry cough. She reports fingers that turn white then blue in the cold and morning hand stiffness. Fine crackles at both bases, no clubbing; SpO2 93% on room air.
correlates.workup: FVC 68% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.85, DLCO 55%. CT: symmetric bilateral lower-lobe fine reticulation with patchy hazy opacities and no cysts. Biopsy: lymphocytes and plasma cells or scarring all at one stage of age; no fibroblast nodules.

correlates.name: Desquamative interstitial pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old man who smokes 1.5 packs a day has 4 months of slowly increasing dyspnea and a dry cough. Fine basal crackles and early clubbing. FVC 76% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.82, DLCO 50%.
correlates.workup: Lung biopsy: alveolar airspaces uniformly packed with brown-pigmented macrophages whose cytoplasm holds lamellar bodies (surfactant debris from dead type II pneumocytes); alveolar walls only mildly thickened.
correlates.management: Stop smoking and start systemic corticosteroids; the response is excellent, though a few go on to scarring.

correlates.name: Respiratory bronchiolitis-associated ILD
correlates.presentation: A 42-year-old man who currently smokes a pack a day (25 pack-years) has a year of mild cough and gradually increasing breathlessness on stairs. A few scattered crackles, no clubbing. FVC 82% predicted, DLCO 68%.
correlates.workup: Lung biopsy: brown-pigmented macrophages packed in the lumens of first- and second-order bronchioles just proximal to the alveolar ducts, with collagen around those bronchioles; the alveoli beyond are spared.
correlates.management: Smoking cessation alone; symptoms and lung function improve once he quits.
